turns.text: still. four paws braced on the monorail platform's maintenance rail, ears swiveled backward instead of forward — the rails hum a half-step off from their usual pitch, some wrongness threaded under the rhythm like a second song bleeding through the first. i don't move yet. i taste it before i place it: copper and ozone, a frequency that sits behind the teeth instead of in the ears.

the platform's overhead lights buzz in their usual cadence, but three meters down the rail a junction box has been cracked open, its cover hanging on one bolt, wires spilling out pale and exposed to the rain. the wrongness you're tasting is coming from there — a signal riding the copper that shouldn't be, looping under the transit system's normal chatter like something's borrowed the frequency and forgot to give it back. a monorail car groans somewhere in the dark tunnel mouth, still ten minutes out. down on the street level, a drone's public-address crackles through standing water: 'CITIZENS ARE REMINDED — bounty active on the loading-dock thief, forty thousand loyalty points, approach with caution, do not attempt personal apprehension.' the announcement loops twice and cuts to static.

*i drop off the rail onto the cracked box, paws finding the one dry patch on its casing.* the signal doesn't smell like anything — that's what's strange. no ozone-burn of a real short, no rubber-melt. just that taste, sour-bright, climbing the back of my tongue every time it pulses. i press one ear flat against the wire bundle. it pulses again, and for half a second the color of the rain changes.

the wire bundle is warm under your ear, warmer than the weather accounts for. the pulse comes again — three seconds apart, steady as a heartbeat — and each time it does, the platform lights flicker one shade toward violet before snapping back. down the line, past where the rail curves into the research district's old maintenance spur, something else is listening too: a shape on the gantry above the tracks, low and still, holding position the way something waits when it already knows what you're about to do. it doesn't move. it doesn't need to.

the shape on the gantry doesn't smell like threat — doesn't smell like much of anything, actually, which is its own kind of wrong. *i follow the pulse instead, down the spur, claws finding old grip-tape worn smooth by decades of boots that weren't mine.* the air changes before the ground does — colder, then sharper, chemical, a smell i know from somewhere i can't place, like a memory that belongs to another mouth.

the spur dead-ends at a service door someone pried and never fixed, hanging open on a stairwell that smells the way old research floors do — solvent, cold metal, an underlayer of something biological gone stale years ago. this used to be a testing level. the walls still carry faint burn-scoring near the baseboards, patch-welded over more than once. whatever ran here left traces in the wiring that never fully cleared — small errors, repeating loops, the pulse you're chasing just one of many ghosts still rattling around in cable nobody's replaced. something skitters in the dark above the doorframe, too many legs for a rat, moving with the jerky precision of a thing that was built rather than born.

*ears pin flat, every hair down my spine standing at once.* not a rat. not alive, not exactly — the movement's wrong, too even, joints clicking on a beat the pulse keeps time with. i back two steps into the stairwell's shadow, weight low, ready to bolt but not yet bolting. whatever's up there hasn't looked down. i don't want to be the thing that makes it look down.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

it looks down. the skittering thing drops half a meter on a thread of cable-turned-web, legs unfolding into a splay of six, lens-eyes catching what little light leaks from the stairwell's emergency strip. a maintenance crawler, corp-issue, the kind that used to patrol relay lines and got left running long after the relay itself went dark — nobody decommissioned it, so it never stopped. it clicks once, twice, aiming a thin red thread of a laser sight across the floor a hand's width from your paws. above, past a broken skylight, a silhouette crosses the gap between roof edges — low, deliberate, twin points of light where its eyes should be catching the same violet flicker the wires keep throwing, gone before it's really there.

*i don't wait to find out if the red thread is a real threat or a toy left running.* i'm already moving, low and fast, past the crawler's reach and into the stairwell proper, claws skidding once on wet metal before catching. behind me the clicking speeds up, frustrated, chasing a target that isn't there anymore. ahead, the pulse is louder now, close, coming from a junction cabinet at the bottom of the stairs with its door hanging by one hinge.

the cabinet's guts are a nest of old cable, half of it corp-standard, half of it patched in with wire that doesn't match any authorized spec — someone's been here before, more than once, splicing in taps that shouldn't exist. the pulse lives at the center of it, a small unmarked relay no bigger than a fish tin, blinking that same violet on its three-second beat. it isn't transmitting outward. it's listening. it has been listening for a long time, patient in a way only machines and certain cats manage, cataloguing everything that passes this junction and holding onto all of it, waiting for someone to come collect.

*i nose the relay once — cold, humming, tasting like nothing and everything at once — then close my teeth around the cable feeding it and bite through.* the pulse stutters, stumbles, dies mid-beat. the violet flicker upstairs cuts out with it. somewhere above, i hear the crawler's clicking stop too, like it lost the rhythm it was walking to.

silence drops fast and total, the kind that makes a building feel bigger than it is. the emergency strip lighting holds steady now, no more flicker, no more violet. footsteps start on the level above — human, unhurried, the particular tread of someone who gets paid whether or not they find anything. down here the cut relay sits dead in your mouth's memory, its casing still warm. the crawler hasn't followed; whatever it was tuned to, it isn't tuned to you. two floors up, a vent exhales stale server-heat and the specific ozone-and-machine-oil smell of a rack room that's been running hot for years without anyone opening the door.

*i carry the relay's severed cable-end a few meters, just far enough to be sure nothing's tracking the taste of it, then drop it behind a support strut and leave it there.* the rack-room smell pulls at something old and familiar — not this place, not tonight, but close enough that my paws want to follow it before the rest of me agrees. i don't. too many ears in this stairwell already.

the footsteps above cross once, pause, cross back — searching without urgency, the sound of someone checking a maintenance log rather than hunting an intruder. the stairwell door at the top groans on its hinge and settles again, unopened. outside the service door you came in through, the rain has thickened, and the platform announcement starts its loop again, fainter now with distance: bounty, forty thousand points, approach with caution. a monorail car finally rattles through overhead, three minutes late, throwing brief light down through the broken skylight before the tunnel swallows it again.

*i go back up the way i came, slower this time, listening for the crawler's click and not finding it.* the platform's cold air after the stairwell's dead-machine warmth feels almost clean. rain's soaked through to skin already, not that it matters now. i shake once, hard, ears first, and the world stops sounding quite so borrowed.

the platform is empty except for standing water and the junction box, wires still spilling out but quiet now, no pulse left to taste. the transit chatter has gone back to its normal register, nothing riding underneath it. far off across the gap between two arcology towers, that same low silhouette holds position on a ledge, watching the district the way something watches territory it's already decided is uninteresting tonight. it doesn't cross toward you. eventually it isn't there at all — you didn't see it leave, just registered, at some point, that the ledge was empty.

*i settle low against the warm side of the junction box, tail wrapped tight, and wait out the last of the rain there.* whatever the relay was cataloguing, it isn't anymore. that'll have to be enough. sleep pulls at the edges anyway, heavy after all that listening, and for once nothing in the wire hum underneath me sounds like it's asking for anything back.

the rain thins to a drizzle, then to nothing, and the district settles into its usual hours-before-dawn hush — distant traffic-glow, a drone's rotor somewhere far south, the monorail's next car still fifteen minutes out. the junction box ticks as it cools. above the tracks, the sky stays the flat orange-grey it always does here, no stars, no dark, just the long unbroken glow of a city that never quite decides to go all the way to sleep. for now, at least, nothing is listening back.
